rv.q: Unfortunately, despite a great deal of charm and intelligence, Amélie doesn’t so much refute the paradox as prove it.
“Amélie” the musical seems to have no nationality, or sensibility, to call its own.
The two duties ultimately cancel each other out.
But overall this show is a lesson in messing with the sacred.

cn.t: This mild-mannered adaptation of the beloved French film fails to inspire the original's passionate responses, delivering a promising but ultimately cloying musical that never fully realizes its stage potential despite Phillipa Soo's appealing performance.

vs.sum: The Walter Kerr Theatre offers excellent sightlines and sound quality, making it a great venue for intimate productions. However, the comfort level is below average due to limited legroom and seat width, though the theater's Italian Renaissance-inspired decor adds to its charm.

acc.note: No elevators. All accessible seating on Orchestra level. Infrared headsets and audio induction neck loops.
